criteria.criterion: A retiring MCP container with 0 in-flight certified ops shuts down within the short DEFAULT_UVICORN_GRACEFUL_SECONDS backstop (not the 1200s op grace), proven by a test asserting timeout_graceful_shutdown == DEFAULT_UVICORN_GRACEFUL_SECONDS < DEFAULT_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS.

A retiring MCP container with >0 in-flight certified ops still receives the full grace_seconds drain and is never cut short, proven by a test asserting should_exit stays False until the gauge reaches 0.

A NEW certified op arriving after SIGTERM (during the drain) is REFUSED (MCPRetiringError) and does not increment the gauge, while an already-in-flight op is unaffected — so a burst cannot re-pin the retiring port for the full grace. Proven by a gauge-level and a handler-level test.
An unreadable /health caused by a mid-redeploy bot yields a DEFER with a countable AUTODEPLOY_DEFERRED bot-redeploying marker and no compose build/up, asserted by the bash harness.

A genuinely wedged/down bot (or an exhausted mid-redeploy defer bound) still fails open, runs compose build, and emits the countable AUTODEPLOY_REVIEW_INTERRUPT signal-unavailable marker, asserted by the bash harness.
No capacity change is made: MCP_RELEASES_CAP and the blue-green port set are unchanged; both fixes are in-process/host-local with no CI-provider dependency.
